metadata.description: Analyze App and Platform availability and monitor the requests and failures to your container app job

Platform maintenance detected during this time window (Platform host OS upgrade)

Azure Container Apps periodically performs platform maintenance to apply security patches, bug fixes, and feature updates. During these maintenance events, application containers are gracefully restarted.

This is expected behavior and does not indicate an application issue. Container restarts during this window are platform-initiated.
Platform maintenance detected during this time window (Platform host OS upgrade)

• If you need more control over when platform maintenance occurs, configure Planned Maintenance to schedule upgrades during preferred time windows
  • Ensure your application handles graceful shutdown signals (SIGTERM) properly — see Container configuration
  • Review the Container Exit Events detector to confirm that container exits during this period have a ManuallyStopped reason and exit code 0, which confirms they are platform-initiated

Both successful and failed job executions found within the specified timeframe

• If DeadlineExceeded is seen, review the Container Apps - Jobs - DeadLineExceeded blog section
    • This may show if a job is taking longer than what is specified in 'Replica Timeout' for the job configuration.
    • This can happen if the application is not running to completion, taking a longer through app logic, or - crashing/exiting, or failing in some other manner enough times that 'Replica timeout' is hit which has precedence over 'Replica retry count'
  • If BackOffLimitExceeded is seen, review the Container Apps - Jobs - BackOffLimitExceeded blog section
    • This can happen if a container (in the job pod) is exiting/crashing with a non-successful status code - such as due to unhandled exceptions or other application errors. This can also happen to due to other issues such as container create failures, image pull failures, or other related issues.
Both successful and failed job executions found within the specified timeframe

• The current log destination for this environment is set to: Log Analytics
  • If the reason for failed job executions are container exits/start failures/or code logic taking too long to execute - query application stdout/err logging in the ContainerAppConsoleLogs_CL table from the Logs blade. This should be done as it may save a large chunk of time in troubleshooting
  • If the reason for failed job executions are moreso due to lifecycle issues (container create failures, image pull issues, etc.) - query pod and container logging in the ContainerAppSystemLogs_CL table from the Logs blade

rows: The below query can be ran to review system logs (pod, container, lifecycle logs, etc.) for the job named system-health within the specified time frame: ``` ContainerAppSystemLogs_CL | where TimeGenerated between (datetime(2026-10-19 22:00:00) .. datetime(2026-10-19 23:00:00)) | where JobName_s =~ 'system-health' | project TimeGenerated, Log_s, ExecutionName_s, Reason_s ``` The below query can be ran to review application stdout/err logs for the job named system-health within the specified time frame: ``` ContainerAppConsoleLogs_CL | where TimeGenerated between (datetime(2026-10-19 22:00:00) .. datetime(2026-10-19 23:00:00)) | where ContainerJobName_s =~ 'system-health' | project TimeGenerated, Log_s, ContainerGroupName_s, ContainerName_s ```

renderingProperties.title: Environment events and properties
renderingProperties.description:
This table shows the following properties:
  • environmentProvisioningState: The provisioning state of the environment. If this is not successful, CRUD operations may fail.
  • managedClusterProvisioningState: The provisioning state of the cluster. If not successful, availability may be affected. Note: The LoadBalancerFrontEndIPMisMatch state is informational noise and does not impact cluster or application availability.
  • powerState: The power state of the cluster.
  • zoneRedundantEnabled: If Zone Redundancy is enabled.
  • logsDestination: Which Log Option is enabled.
  • subnetResourceId: The subnet resource ID used (if VNET).
  • hasPrivateEndpoints: If Private Endpoints is enabled.
  • publicNetworkAccess: If public network access is enabled.
  • hasMaintenanceConfiguration: If Planned Maintenance is enabled.
